messages:
maya: Quick q — for per-org limits should we combine RPM and TPM + concurrency, or pick one as primary? Thinking about burst credits + fallback to lower-tier model.
grant: I'd prefer RPM+concurrency combo. RPM handles long tail, concurrency prevents spikes.
sara: Agree. Also we need a clear SLO mapping in console so customers can see token vs req metrics.
alex: Two caveats: 1) TPM is more natural for token billing, 2) concurrency enforcement is tricky across dedicated pools.
maya: Right. Maybe rule: primary is RPM/TPM pair (both enforced), concurrency as soft cap with queueing + 429 after grace credits.
grant: +1 for soft cap. Suggest implement burst credits bucket that refills at RPM rate, separate for tokens and requests.
sara: UI note: show current credit level and last refill time in console, add tooltip about starvation.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled for feature/ratelimit-refactor at 05:30 UTC
alex: Also need telemetry: sampling for 429s, histograms for wait times, and breakdown by model+region.
maya: Can someone prototype config DSL? e.g.

```
org_rate {
  rpm: 1200
  tpm: 20000
  concurrency_soft: 30
  burst_tokens: 5000
}
```

grant: looks good. let's sync tomorrow 11am. :calendar:
sara: I'll add a short mock to the console PR, include the credit gauge.
maya: thanks. assigning followups: @grant prototyping token bucket impl, @sara console mock, @alex infra edge cases doc.
grant: on it.
